tasks.title: Promote the customer-schema migration: two relations, their checks, keys and the partial unique Main-address index
tasks.dod: The staged migration is promoted to apps/server/migrations/1786700000000-CreateCustomerSchema.ts, applies and reverts cleanly against the development database, and repository integration tests assert per-Warehouse customer-name uniqueness across active and Inactive, the same name accepted in two Warehouses, and the at-most-one-Main-address partial unique index refusing a concurrent second mark.

tasks.title: Promote the delivery-destinations migration: 14 columns across five shipped relations, with the Via Warehouse and ending-attribution backfills
tasks.dod: The staged migration is promoted to apps/server/migrations/1786700100000-AddDeliveryDestinations.ts, applies and reverts cleanly against a development database holding pre-existing purchase_draft_lines and customer_orders rows, every existing line reads delivery_mode = via_warehouse before the column is made NOT NULL, customer_orders.customer_name drops NOT NULL with chk_customer_orders_customer_identity satisfied on its typed-name side by every existing row, and the down path's two data repairs are exercised rather than assumed.

tasks.title: Promote the Permission grant migration and add the feature's PermissionId, WorkspacePermissionId and ErrorCode members
tasks.dod: The staged migration is promoted to apps/server/migrations/1786700200000-GrantDeliveryAddressPermissions.ts, applies and reverts cleanly, idempotently inserts the four Warehouse Permissions and one Workspace Permission and grants each to its protected Role, and packages/shared-types exports CUSTOMERS:WATCH/:CREATE/:UPDATE/:DEACTIVATE, WAREHOUSES:ADDRESS_UPDATE and every customers.* ErrorCode plus the customer_orders.* and purchase_drafts.* additions with the shipped workspace and ordering suites still green.

tasks.title: Add the two new shared persistence entities and extend the four shipped ones, registered on DomainModule
tasks.dod: CustomerEntity and CustomerDeliveryAddressEntity map to the migrated relations and each carries the warehouse_id its ownership rule needs; CustomerOrderEntity, PurchaseDraftLineEntity, DemandSnapshotEntryEntity and WarehouseEntity carry their added columns; DomainModule resolves every one of them; and an integration test round-trips a row of each new and each changed entity.

tasks.title: Add @ObservedPermission, resolve it in WarehouseAccessGuard, and carry observedPermissionIds on AccessCurrentUser
tasks.dod: Guard unit tests prove an ungranted observed Permission never denies, an ungranted required Permission still denies, the observed set on the principal is exactly the granted subset, a handler declaring only observed Permissions and no required one is still denied, and archived handling plus the ambiguous-warehouseId refusal are unchanged; AccessCurrentUser stays frozen, gains a readonly observedPermissionIds that is empty when nothing is declared, and is still never returned to the browser.

tasks.title: Build the customers domain: value objects, predicates, error factories, mappers and CustomerAddressBookService
tasks.dod: Unit tests cover the blank-name and blank-address rules, name availability across active and Inactive alike, the last-active-address condition, Main-address membership and the reassignment CustomerAddressBookService performs when the current Main one is deactivated; the directory imports no NestJS, HTTP or TypeORM symbol, and CustomerAddressBookService is registered on the UsecaseModule and not exported.

tasks.title: Add the three customers specialized repositories: directory, address book and awaiting demand
tasks.dod: CustomerDirectoryRepository returns name availability and the Customer list with active-address counts in one read; CustomerAddressBookRepository performs the address set read, the Main-address transition and the last-active-address condition under lock; CustomerAwaitingDemandRepository returns one Customer's Unfulfilled orders with Item, Outstanding Quantity, needed-by date and destination; each is covered by repository integration tests, exposes no private methods and imports no feature module.

tasks.title: Add the Customer lifecycle commands: record, correct the name, deactivate and reactivate
tasks.dod: Use-case unit tests against controlled repository doubles prove a Customer is recorded active with its first address as Main together with the recording attribution, a blank name or address is refused naming the value, a taken name is refused naming the Customer that holds it whether active or Inactive, the same name is accepted in a second Warehouse, a correction to an unused name leaves every naming Customer Order and frozen line reading as before, deactivation keeps the name taken and every address in the state it was already in, and a Customer of another Warehouse is refused identically to one that does not exist.

tasks.title: Add the Delivery Address book commands: add, revise, mark Main, deactivate and reactivate
tasks.dod: Use-case unit tests prove a second address is recorded with its access notes and marking it Main clears the previous Main one, exactly one active address is Main at rest, deactivating an address leaves every naming Customer Order and frozen line reading and counting as before, deactivating the Main one promotes a remaining active address and reports which, the last active address is refused under lock with the add-first guidance, and an address of another Customer or another Warehouse is refused identically to a missing one.

tasks.title: Serve the customers REST surface with its queries and the new @warehouser/contracts/customers subpath
tasks.dod: The list, one-Customer-with-awaiting and picker queries are served by the eleven operations across seven paths openapi.yaml defines under api/v1/warehouses/{warehouseId}/customers; contract tests prove each validates its shared schema, is denied without its Permission and permitted with it, denies non-disclosingly for a Customer of another Warehouse, refuses every mutation on an archived Warehouse while every read succeeds, and presents no count anywhere to a member lacking CUSTOMERS:WATCH; reads declare @ArchivedTolerantRead(), writes declare @WriteRateLimited(), and each controller declares exactly one @RequiredPermission.

tasks.title: Record the Warehouse's own Delivery Address end to end: Workspace-guarded command, route, contract and detail-pane section
tasks.dod: PUT /api/v1/workspace/warehouses/{warehouseId}/delivery-address records and corrects the address and its access notes under WAREHOUSES:ADDRESS_UPDATE through WorkspaceAccessGuard, never deactivates, and is denied without the Workspace Permission; the Delivery address section renders between the warehouse-name form and the people list behind WorkspacePermissionGate, absent rather than disabled without the Permission; and the address is readable from the Warehouse-scoped draft projections without any Workspace Role.

tasks.title: Give a Customer Order its destination and add the redirection command
tasks.dod: Use-case unit tests prove recording a Customer Order against a Customer defaults to that Customer's Main Delivery Address and honours a stated active one, a typed customer name records with no Customer and no address and is neither matched nor created, RedirectCustomerOrderCommand moves an Unfulfilled order under lock and refuses an address of another Customer, an Inactive address, and a Fulfilled or cancelled order, and a Customer or address of another Warehouse is refused without disclosing that it exists elsewhere.

tasks.title: Redact customer identity in the demand and Customer Order projections and serve their REST surface
tasks.dod: A redaction unit test per projection proves that without CUSTOMERS:WATCH the customer name, Delivery Address and access notes are absent from the response rather than null, that a typed name is withheld exactly as a Customer's name is, that no count survives, and that everything the member's own Permissions admit is unchanged; the demand, Customer Order list, amendment and redirection endpoints declare @ObservedPermission(CUSTOMERS:WATCH) and validate both the redacted and the unredacted contract shape.

tasks.title: Extend the purchase-drafts domain with Delivery Mode, the ending rules and the closure predicate
tasks.dod: Unit tests prove a Direct to Customer line never names the Warehouse's own Delivery Address, a new line starts as Via Warehouse, an ending matches its line's delivery mode in both directions, an ending is recorded at most once, and the closure predicate holds exactly when every line of a draft has an ending; error factories exist for a mode or address change after freeze, a disagreeing link set, a missing Warehouse Delivery Address, a wrong-mode ending and a repeated ending.

tasks.title: Set a line's Delivery Mode and Delivery Address, and enforce the direct-line agreement at the link and the revision
tasks.dod: PurchaseDraftAssemblyService gains one shared disagreeing-link read invoked by the link command and the line-revision command; use-case unit tests prove a direct line is refused a link to demand going anywhere else, a revision that would strand existing links is refused naming every disagreement and withdrawing none, a Via Warehouse line runs no such check and keeps ordering's loose linking with unreconciled quantities, and naming the Warehouse's own address on a direct line is refused.

tasks.title: Freeze the delivery statement by value and refuse the two conditions that make a freeze unsound
tasks.dod: Moving a draft to Ready for Ordering captures each line's Delivery Address text, access notes and customer name and each Demand Snapshot entry's captured Delivery Address as they read at that instant; integration tests prove a later edit of the source address does not move a captured value, the transition is refused when a Via Warehouse line's Warehouse has no Delivery Address while adding and revising lines on that draft still works, the transition is refused on a disagreeing link set naming every disagreement, and no live address reference survives on a frozen line for an edit to travel along.

tasks.title: Replace the whole-draft arrival with per-line endings and withdraw POST /purchase-drafts/{id}/arrival
tasks.dod: ConfirmPurchaseDraftLineArrivalCommand and RecordPurchaseDraftLineDeliveryCommand replace ConfirmPurchaseDraftArrivalCommand and are served at the two per-line sub-resources while the whole-draft arrival route is gone from the regenerated route-table baseline; command integration tests prove one line's ending writes its quantity, its Allocations and every resulting Outstanding Quantity together or not at all under an injected mid-way failure, an ending against the wrong mode and a second ending on one line are refused naming when and by whom, the draft stays Ready for Ordering until the last line has an ending and moves to Closed exactly then, closing with a reason still closes whatever lines remain unrecorded, and no Item's On-hand Quantity changes on either ending.

tasks.title: Report Address Drift and serve the by-line split from the read repository
tasks.dod: PurchaseDraftReadRepository computes each Drift Signal as a value comparison between the captured Demand Snapshot address and the Customer Order now, storing nothing and repairing nothing, so a redirection is reflected on the next read and reporting stops once the order is redirected back; integration tests cover many links per draft and many drafts per Warehouse, prove every frozen value is left untouched, and the by-line projection returns each frozen line under the Delivery Mode that places it.

tasks.title: Serve the purchase-drafts REST surface: line delivery, readiness, the by-line read and the redacted draft reads
tasks.dod: Every purchase-draft endpoint openapi.yaml defines validates its shared schema and maps its stable refusal; the draft list, one draft and GET /purchase-draft-lines declare @ObservedPermission(CUSTOMERS:WATCH) and serve both the redacted and the unredacted shape; contract tests prove no frozen delivery column is reachable through the redirection, ending or closure payload, every mutation is denied on an archived Warehouse while every read succeeds, and the regenerated route-table baseline serves no method-and-path pair twice.

tasks.title: Add the architecture check that ties an identity-bearing response schema to its observed-Permission declaration
tasks.dod: A static check reads the resolved handler metadata and the contract schemas and fails when any read whose response schema can carry a customer-identity field does not declare @ObservedPermission(CUSTOMERS:WATCH); it enumerates the identity-bearing surfaces from the spec §1 inventory rather than from memory, and companion checks prove controllers call use cases only, customers domain code imports no framework, no module imports another module's domain errors, predicates or DTOs, shared repositories import no feature module, and customers does not import purchase-drafts.

tasks.title: Build the Customers web destination with its address book, awaiting list, dialogs and the shared customer picker
tasks.dod: modules/customer renders the approved frames KRDln and b7gaH9 with the Customer Card, Address Row, Awaiting Row and Awaiting Card Mobile components, its loader dispatches nothing without CUSTOMERS:WATCH and the sidebar entry is absent rather than disabled, the address and access notes render as text and never as markup or a link, the customer and address picker is exposed on the module's declared public surface, en/uk keys reach full parity with the locale baseline regenerated in its existing key order, and pnpm --filter @warehouser/web build passes with both contracts aliases in place.

tasks.title: Carry the destination onto the Demand surface and add the redirect dialog
tasks.dod: The demand row and its mobile card carry the destination line, the record dialog gains the customer and address fields through the picker modules/customer exposes, and a redirect dialog is added; component tests prove the map-pin is never rendered for a typed-name order and the accompanying text carries the same meaning for a screen reader, identity is withheld across the whole surface for a member holding CUSTOMER_ORDERS:WATCH but not CUSTOMERS:WATCH, a redirection invalidates the tags that feed the drift view, cache entries are keyed per Warehouse, and en/uk parity holds with the locale baseline regenerated.

tasks.title: Add the per-line DELIVERY block, the drift presentation split by mode, and the By-line view
tasks.dod: The draft line renders the DELIVERY block with its radiogroup mode control at both viewports and the frozen line uses the HeroUI disabled field treatment rather than a read-only lookalike; drift is reported on the draft list card for a direct line and inside the opened draft for a via-warehouse line, instructing nothing and blocking nothing; the By draft / By line toggle renders the Dock Line Row split; delivery mode and ending state are total Record render lookups with no conditional ladder; identity is withheld without CUSTOMERS:WATCH; archived Warehouses render read-only; and en/uk parity holds with the locale baseline regenerated.

tasks.title: Replace the whole-draft arrival modal with the two 720px per-line ending dialogs
tasks.dod: ConfirmArrivalDialog is replaced by the arrival and direct-delivery dialogs, each 720px, each reusing the link row as its assignment row, each offered only for the line's own delivery mode and refused independently by the server when it is not; success copy states the outcome that committed and its invisible consequence that a direct delivery moved no stock; no call to the withdrawn whole-draft arrival endpoint remains anywhere in apps/web; and pnpm --filter @warehouser/web build passes.

tasks.title: Raise the ordering change request and promote @ObservedPermission into docs/system
tasks.dod: docs/change-requests/ records the four amendments this feature makes to the approved ordering specification — the narrowed loose-linking boundary, the crossed ends-where-the-goods-arrive non-goal, the per-line closure replacing the once-per-draft one, and the extended Demand Snapshot — so a reviewer reading ordering alone no longer finds it contradicted; and the observed-Permission stage is documented in docs/system with server-index.md updated in the same change, so the two-level authorization stage is not left incompletely described.
